learningObjective: Create and secure a container registry, build and push images, and run containers on ACI and Container Apps with the right sign-in, networking, restart and revision settings.
engineer: Azure Container Registry (ACR) names: 5 to 50 letters and numbers, unique across Azure (<name>.azurecr.io).
ACR tiers (SKUs): Basic, Standard and Premium differ in storage and speed. Only Premium has geo-replication, private endpoints, content trust and dedicated agent pools.
Building images: in the cloud with az acr build (ACR Tasks, no Docker needed on your machine), or locally with docker push after az acr login.

Signing in to ACR: Entra identities with the AcrPull or AcrPush role (managed identities for Azure services, service principals for CI pipelines); repository-scoped tokens; the admin user, which is off by default, is one shared password, and isn't recommended. Anonymous pull is an option on Standard and Premium.
Azure Container Instances (ACI), the container group: the unit you deploy. Its containers run on the same host and share network, lifecycle and volumes. Groups with several containers are Linux only.

ACI settings: CPU and memory per container; OS type; ports; a public IP with an optional DNS name (<label>.<region>.azurecontainer.io), or a private IP in a VNet subnet; environment variables, with secure values for secrets; Azure Files volumes.

ACI restart policy: Always, the default, restarts the container every time it stops; OnFailure restarts only if it fails; Never doesn't restart. For jobs that should finish and stop, use OnFailure or Never.
ACI and a private registry: it needs registry credentials or a managed identity with AcrPull.
Container Apps, the environment: apps run in a Container Apps environment, which shares a VNet and logging.
Container Apps ingress: external (internet) or internal (VNet only), with a target port, and HTTPS automatically.

Container Apps revisions: a revision is a saved, unchangeable version of the app. Changing the image, containers or scale rules creates a new one. Single revision mode replaces the old revision. Multiple revision mode lets you split traffic between revisions (blue/green, canary).
Container Apps extras: secrets; managed identities; Dapr; jobs.

Which one to pick: ACI for a simple single container or a batch job; Container Apps for web APIs, microservices and event-driven apps that need scaling and revisions; AKS when you need full control of Kubernetes.

example.title: A nightly job and a public API
body: A nightly clean-up container runs on ACI with restart policy OnFailure. It stops when it's done, so you only pay while it runs. It pulls its image from ACR using a user-assigned managed identity that has AcrPull.
The public API runs on Container Apps with external ingress. Version 2 is deployed as a new revision and gets 20% of the traffic. After checking it works, the team moves traffic to 100%.

architectureDecisions: Build in the cloud with ACR Tasks: build agents don't need Docker installed.
Pull with managed identities: keep the admin user off.
Several regions: use Premium ACR with geo-replication.

misconceptions.reality: No. ACI has no autoscale. Use Container Apps or AKS.

misconceptions.myth: The ACR admin user is the recommended way to pull images.
misconceptions.reality: No. Use Entra identities with AcrPull.

misconceptions.myth: Every change to a container app creates a new revision.
misconceptions.reality: No. Only revision-scope changes do (image, containers, scale rules).

comparisons.difference: Full Kubernetes: you manage node pools and the cluster. Container Apps hides Kubernetes from you.

comparisons.service: AWS ECR / ECS on Fargate / App Runner
comparisons.difference: ECR is like ACR. Fargate tasks are like ACI. App Runner and ECS services are like Container Apps.

troubleshooting.symptom: ACI is stuck pulling the image: unauthorized.
troubleshooting.cause: No credentials or identity for the private registry.
troubleshooting.fix: Give the managed identity AcrPull and pass --acr-identity, or give registry credentials.

troubleshooting.symptom: An ACI batch job keeps running again and again.
A container app can't be reached from the internet.
troubleshooting.cause: Ingress is internal or off, or the target port is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on external ingress with the port the container listens on.

troubleshooting.symptom: A new revision gets no traffic.
troubleshooting.cause: Multiple revision mode, with traffic fixed on the old revision.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the traffic weights, or send traffic to the latest revision.

configuration.limits: ACR name: 5 to 50 letters and numbers
ACI resources are fixed per container group (redeploy to change them)
configuration.permissions: Contributor, to create registries and apps
AcrPush for CI pipelines, AcrPull for apps that run images
User Access Administrator or Owner, to give AcrPull
configuration.prerequisites: A resource group, and a Dockerfile or an image
For VNet deployment: a delegated subnet (ACI) or an environment VNet (Container Apps)
